prompt: Produce ONE SQUARE art sheet divided exactly into four equal square postcards in a clean regular 2 by 2 grid, NO margins, NO gutters, no borders, no text on any of them. Each square is an independent hand-painted still life with its own colorway, filling all of that quadrant, and the cuts at perfect center horizontally and vertically. Intimate warm midcentury storybook gouache and wax colored-pencil illustrations, flat inky shadows, visibly printed paper grain, gentle handmade uneven edges. Limited coordinated pigments from ochre, faded coral, thyme green, ultramarine and plum. They are keepsakes for a student's personal illustrated journal. TOP LEFT: a single close-up black rubber intake roller with clear axle and red timing belt on a small frame for a student-built competition robot, with one small red hex key on a periwinkle workshop table. Believable small mechanism, cropped close, soft diagonal sunlight, no futuristic robots. TOP RIGHT: a pale yellow and lilac branching particle-collision event display, fine radiating tracks and three strong perfectly plausible curved particle trails captured on a deep midnight teal square piece of scientific graph paper; gorgeous quietly luminous screenprint, one small pink dot at the center. BOTTOM LEFT: cozy school computing workshop, only an old mint green computer monitor viewed close with small cream block cursor on charcoal display, a pencil and a rich orange notebook below it, dusty peach studio wall, no letters or words. BOTTOM RIGHT: a single dark plum translucent cassette tape with two winding reels, lilac label with no words and a tiny hand-drawn star sticker, on a rose red table with a curling golden ribbon of tape and the corner of a pale blue paper sleeve. No labels, no typography, no numbers, no watermark. Each illustration should feel tactile, personal, deliberately composed from life. Separate quadrants at the exact midlines to allow programmatic cutting into four small paintings.
